title: Financial record versus accounts payable
summary: Choose the flow based on whether cash has already moved or the debt is still pending.
guidance: Use financial record when the church already paid or received the money
Use accounts payable when the debt exists first and will be paid later
Use accounts receivable when the church expects to receive money in the future

title: Reuse an existing financial concept before creating a new one
summary: Financial concepts should be reusable and not overly specific to one isolated case.
guidance: Prefer an existing concept when it already describes the transaction well
Create a new concept only when no existing concept fits the use case
Names and descriptions should be general enough to reuse in future records

title: Outgoing movements usually need cost center context
summary: Outgoing financial records are commonly tied to a cost center to classify where the expense belongs.
guidance: If the concept type is outgoing, review whether a cost center is required
Use cost centers to organize ministry, project or area expenses

title: Internal transfer is not a normal expense
summary: Transfers between availability accounts should use the internal transfer flow instead of a regular expense record.
guidance: Use internal transfer when money only moves between church accounts
Do not classify internal transfers as normal income or expense

title: Church assets should go to patrimony when they need lifecycle control
summary: Use patrimony for church goods that need identification, tracking, inventory or disposal history instead of treating them as a simple expense flow.
guidance: Use patrimony when the church is registering a durable good, equipment, furniture or another asset that should be tracked over time
Use a normal financial or purchase flow only when you need the accounting registration without asset lifecycle management
If the user asks about church goods, patrimony is usually the first module to review

title: Purchase flow should be used when invoice and item control matter
summary: Use the purchases module when the user needs invoice attachment, supplier context or itemized purchase handling beyond a simple cash posting.
guidance: Use purchases when the transaction belongs to the purchasing workflow and should keep invoice context
Use a normal financial record when a simple accounting posting is enough
If the purchase results in a durable church asset, also review patrimony registration

title: Bank statement reconciliation is a review flow, not a normal posting flow
summary: Imported statements and reconciliation should be handled in banking screens, while accounting registration happens in the appropriate financial flow.
guidance: Use bank statements when the user needs to import, review or reconcile bank movements
Do not treat reconciliation as the same thing as creating a new financial record
If a bank movement is unmatched, review whether the accounting entry already exists or must be created

title: Some registrations depend on prior financial configuration
summary: Before registering movements, the church may need financial concepts, availability accounts, banks or cost centers already configured.
guidance: If the user cannot continue a flow, verify whether concepts, accounts, banks or cost centers are missing
Availability accounts are needed to register cash or bank impact
Cost centers are commonly needed for outgoing classifications

title: Member contribution review is different from direct treasury registration
summary: Use contributions list to review contributions submitted through the member flow, but use financial record when treasury is manually registering money that already entered cash or bank.
guidance: Use financial record when the church already received the money and treasury is posting it directly
Use contributions list only when the contribution was submitted through the online or member contribution flow and needs review or status update
If the user asks for a specific concept such as primicia, only recommend it when that concept exists in the church financial concepts delivered in context
If no suitable concept is found, guide the user to review the financial concepts list before creating a new concept

title: Suppliers should exist before some purchase or payable flows
summary: Purchases and payable registrations may require a supplier to exist first.
guidance: If the supplier is missing, create it before continuing the purchase or payable flow
Avoid creating duplicate suppliers when one already exists

title: Bank setup and availability account setup are related but different
summary: A bank is institutional configuration, while availability accounts are the accounts used directly in postings and balances.
guidance: Configure the bank when the banking institution is missing from system setup
Configure the availability account when the church needs the account to appear in financial postings or balance views
Some flows may depend on both being correctly configured

title: Financial month status can block operational postings
summary: Some accounting actions depend on the financial month being open or administratively available.
guidance: If the user cannot post in a period, verify whether the financial month is open
Use financial month management for period control rather than bypassing the accounting status

title: Some purchases also need patrimony follow-up
summary: A purchase may be correctly registered in the purchases module and still require patrimony registration if the result is a durable church asset.
guidance: Use purchases to record supplier, invoice and item details
If the purchased item is durable and should be inventoried, also review patrimony registration

title: Paying an account payable is different from creating the commitment
summary: The payable flow creates the obligation first; the cash movement happens later when the installment is settled.
guidance: Create the payable when the debt exists but is still unpaid
When the installment is actually paid, the treasury flow should settle that commitment instead of creating a brand new unrelated expense
Avoid duplicating the same obligation as both a payable and a separate direct expense

title: Collecting an account receivable is different from creating the receivable
summary: The receivable flow tracks future income, while the actual receipt should respect the collection or settlement flow when money is received.
guidance: Create the receivable when the church expects to receive money later
When the money is effectively collected, avoid duplicating the same future income as a separate unrelated receivable
Review whether the operational flow should settle the receivable instead of registering a disconnected new commitment

title: Some support issues are really permission or access issues
summary: When a user cannot see or execute a flow, the cause may be missing role permissions instead of financial misconfiguration.
guidance: Review roles and permissions when the user reports missing menus or blocked actions
Review users and access when the issue is specific to one user account
Do not treat access-control problems as accounting configuration problems

title: Cash-impact postings depend on an availability account
summary: Whenever the movement changes treasury or bank balance, the posting should identify the availability account used in that operation.
guidance: Use the availability account that actually received or paid the money
If the needed account does not exist, configure it first before posting
Do not confuse bank institutional setup with the account used directly in treasury postings

title: Member commitments are not the same as direct treasury receipts
summary: A member commitment belongs to the receivable or member flow, while a treasury receipt is a cash posting that already happened.
guidance: Use member commitments or accounts receivable for future obligations tied to members
Use financial record when the church already received the money in cash or bank
Avoid registering the same member obligation twice in both flows

title: Bank reconciliation depends on prior bank setup
summary: If the banking institution or related setup is missing, the user should configure the bank before expecting reconciliation to work correctly.
guidance: Create the bank when the institution is missing from system setup
Then review whether the availability account linked to that treasury or bank account also exists
Only after the setup is complete should the user continue with statement import or reconciliation

title: Church profile settings are different from financial configuration
summary: Institutional church data belongs to the church profile, while treasury and accounting behavior belong to financial configuration modules.
guidance: Use church profile for institutional data and church-level information
Use financial concepts, accounts, banks and cost centers for treasury configuration
Do not treat profile settings as if they were accounting setup

title: Benevolence should not be treated like a normal recurring operating expense
summary: Support given to a family, member or person in need is usually a targeted assistance flow rather than a routine operating expense of the church.
guidance: Treat benevolence as a specific outgoing aid or assistance case, not as a normal recurring office expense
Use an existing benevolence or assistance concept if the church already has one configured
If no suitable concept exists, review concepts before forcing the registration into a generic OPEX concept

title: A payment to a guest minister or musician depends on the event context
summary: Payments to invited preachers or musicians should be evaluated according to whether they belong to a specific event, a ministry transfer or an exceptional support case.
guidance: If the guest payment is tied directly to a specific event or conference, compare it against event-related concepts first
If the payment is truly exceptional and non-recurring, avoid forcing it into a normal recurring operating concept
If the church treats this kind of disbursement as a ministry transfer, use that concept only when the configured concepts and local policy support it

title: Loans, donations and future receivables are different financial cases
summary: The assistant should not confuse a loan granted, a donation received and an amount expected in the future because each one belongs to a different accounting intention.
guidance: Use accounts receivable when the church expects to collect money later
Use a donation or contribution concept only when the money is not expected back
When the church grants or recovers a loan, avoid classifying that movement as a normal offering or expense

title: Partial payments should continue the original commitment when one exists
summary: If the church already created a payable or receivable, partial settlements should normally follow that original commitment instead of creating disconnected duplicate records.
guidance: If only part of an installment was paid or collected, prefer the settlement flow of the original commitment
Avoid creating multiple unrelated direct records for the same payable or receivable obligation
Use direct treasury posting only when there is no prior commitment controlling that balance

title: A closed month should be treated as a period-control issue, not as a posting shortcut
summary: When the user cannot register a movement because the month is closed, the correct action is to review financial month status instead of bypassing the period control.
guidance: If the posting period is closed, review financial months first
Do not recommend creating records in another module just to avoid period control
Treat this as an administrative or accounting-control issue, not as a concept-classification issue

title: A received loan should not be treated like a normal contribution or offering
summary: When the church receives money that must be returned later, the movement should not be classified as tithe, offering or donation income.
guidance: Do not classify borrowed money as a normal contribution or recurring income concept
If the church received a loan that must be repaid later, review whether the case belongs to a liability or controlled commitment flow
Use direct treasury posting only when cash already entered and the configured concept correctly represents that borrowed-money scenario

title: Event spending should be distinguished from recurring ministry spending
summary: An isolated congress, conference or guest activity should not automatically be classified the same way as the church's ordinary recurring ministry expense.
guidance: If the disbursement belongs to a specific event, retreat or conference, compare event-related concepts first
If the spending is part of recurring ministry operation, compare ordinary recurring concepts instead
Avoid using a generic recurring OPEX concept just because the exact event concept is still unclear
